clue.text: Poor fellow with no company!

parts.note: reads as pity for a friendless man, but describes a person who prefers to act alone, like a pack animal that strays from its pack

explanation.surface: A sympathetic sigh for a man who has nobody to keep him company.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary operator who shuns groups is likened to a wild canine living apart from the pack.

clue.text: Lumbered, and entered into the records

definitions.meaning: felled trees for timber, i.e. worked as a lumberjack
written down in an official book such as a ship's journal

explanation.definitionFit: Lumbering is felling timber, and to log is also to note something formally in a journal.

clue.text: Lifted an employment article with qualms

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the word an is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: employment of something is its use
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone uneasy about raising a point concerning a job and an article.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualms can mean a sick, queasy feeling, the sense of stomach sickness.

clue.text: Refuse to start diet, being emaciated

parts.note: refuse (rubbish) is waste

indicators.note: the start of the word diet is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dieter who refuses to begin eating properly ends up skin and bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wasted is gaunt and thin from illness or hunger.

clue.text: Word for the French car test — only English!

parts.note: le is French for the
the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles
only means just

explanation.surface: Someone asking what the French call a vehicle inspection, adding that only English will do.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the yearly roadworthiness test required for cars in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means the exactly right expression, the perfect term for the occasion.

clue.text: Opera enjoyed by mechanics

definitions.meaning: Bizet's opera about a Spanish gypsy
garage workers, read as men who work on cars

explanation.surface: An opera that is a favourite with garage workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizet's famous opera bears this title, and split in two it describes motor engineers.

clue.text: A cunning ruse admits carpeting sportsmen

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece goes inside the other
a cunning ruse is artfully twisted, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a mat is a piece of floor carpeting

explanation.surface: A crafty trick lets someone in on the carpet trade, oddly about sportsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' looks like a verb (scolding) but supplies a floor covering; 'cunning' scrambles the ruse and 'admits' slips the covering in after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurs are those who play sport unpaid, as non-professionals.

clue.text: The pitfalls of keeping quiet during religious incantations

indicators.note: during means the quiet letter falls within the incantations

parts.note: mantras are chanted sacred phrases
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: Warning of the dangers of staying silent through sacred chanting.
explanation.definitionFit: Traps set to catch people, hence figurative snares and pitfalls.

clue.text: Well known smell found on car seat, oddly

parts.note: to nose is to smell or sniff

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of car seat

explanation.surface: A familiar odour detected on a car's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is widely known, it is no hidden matter at all.

clue.text: Matured vocally a little bit, but ghastly

indicators.note: vocally means the word for matured is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: matured means grew up
some means a little, a bit

explanation.surface: Something that has ripened a little, though it looks dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Grisly and horrifying things are ghastly.

clue.text: Relations on hospital visits

indicators.note: on means placed after, the relations follow the hospital letter

parts.note: aunts are relations

explanation.surface: Family members dropping in on a hospital patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost frequents or visits a place it is said to haunt.

clue.text: W.H.O are giving the weather

definitions.meaning: W, H and O are the chemical symbols for tungsten, hydrogen and oxygen
exposed to wind and rain, as in braving the outdoors

explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten, hydrogen and oxygen are chemical substances of the periodic table, and wind and rain are nature's forces.

clue.text: Chap who spoke out loud? Almost wealthy

indicators.note: out loud means the word for spoke is heard, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: spoke means said

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: A fellow who talks loudly and is very nearly rich.
explanation.walkthrough: SAID heard aloud gives CED; 'Almost' drops the last letter of RICH, leaving RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, so any fellow called by it.

clue.text: Talk of lost sheep is true

indicators.note: talk of means the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: stray means lost and a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Chatter about a missing animal from the flock, claimed to be genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: A tup is a dialect word, common in northern England, for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for honestly, genuinely: said to vouch that a claim is genuine.

clue.text: Stage prop that requires a due script to be rewritten

indicators.note: a script rewritten has its letters reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre prop whose use demands that an overdue script be redrafted.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy pie thrown in slapstick comedy is a classic theatrical property.

clue.text: Prisoner found in rotten piles of liquid waste

indicators.note: found in means placed inside
rotten suggests decay, so the word piles is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A convict discovered among decaying heaps of sewage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid waste' is the definition, not part of the prison picture; 'rotten' scrambles the heap and 'found in' lodges the convict inside it. Lag is British slang for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: A spilt quantity of fluid is liquid lost or wasted.

clue.text: Venture covering English legislation in part of America

indicators.note: covering means one piece wraps round the others

parts.note: to venture is to dare
law is legislation

explanation.surface: A risky enterprise involving English statutes somewhere in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state on the east coast, so a part of the American nation.

clue.text: Proceed, being late, drunk, wearing medal

indicators.note: wearing means the medal is put on round the other letters

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or decoration

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy, so the letters of late are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone moving on, late and tipsy, still sporting a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles the late letters, and 'wearing' has the medal wrapped round them; gong is British slang for a medal or honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To make progress or carry on is to proceed.

clue.text: Contemporary award given to American lawyer on the 4th of July

parts.note: to present is to award, give formally
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

indicators.note: the 4th of picks the fourth letter of the word July

explanation.surface: A prize handed to a US attorney on Independence Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the current era, modern, as things of today are.

clue.text: Powerful company man

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A forceful man who works for a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A forceful, convincing argument is a strong or powerful one.

clue.text: Compiler found in entrance to cell

indicators.note: found in means placed inside

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
the compiler, the setter, refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter discovered at the door to a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves 'compiler' or 'setter' to clue ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproductive cell, such as a sperm or egg, used in fertilisation.

clue.text: Complaints after a good man snaps

indicators.note: after means the complaints come behind the good man

parts.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
complaints are ailments, ills

explanation.surface: Grievances following a decent fellow who loses his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographs from a film are frames, snapshots of a scene.

clue.text: Adult taken in by backing little animals

indicators.note: taken in by means placed inside
backing means the word is reversed

parts.note: little means small
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up deceived by those supporting tiny creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the word for little round, and 'taken in by' sets the adult letter just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: South American pack beasts of the camel family.

clue.text: Inexperienced Italian bloke lost his head with worker

indicators.note: lost his head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: signor is an Italian man, Mr
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: An Italian man beheaded beside a labourer, both naive.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking knowledge or experience means being unknowing.

clue.text: Flower girl prepared to fight

definitions.meaning: something that flows, i.e. a river; the great South American river
a female warrior of Greek legend

explanation.definitionFit: The great South American river is a flower in the sense of something that flows, and the legendary female warriors bear the same name.

clue.text: Heavenly ale brewed over there

indicators.note: over means the jumbled letters sit over, round, the other word
brewed means the ale is stirred up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A divine beer made in some faraway place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' is a container here, not a link: the brewed ale wraps round the word there, its first letter in front and the other two behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate and otherworldly, as though of the sky or celestial realm.

clue.text: Go green, cooking with yoghurt at first

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of green are worked up into a new order
at first means take the opening letter of yoghurt

explanation.surface: An urge to become environmentally friendly by cooking with yoghurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' turns GREEN into ENERG; 'at first' adds Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Go means vigour or get-up-and-go, liveliness and drive.

clue.text: Very clean spades no grass!

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades
pot and grass are both slang for cannabis
less means without, as in no

explanation.surface: A gardener's spade with not a blade of grass on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No grass' reads as a phrase meaning without cannabis, so the word for no comes after the slang for grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Immaculate, without a mark or stain.
